title: WHERE YOUR PAYCHECK ACTUALLY GOES
_doc: Script + storyboard for one explainer. Written to the classical structure Dre specified: WHAT it is, HOW it works, WHY it matters, with one problem and one solution. Every shot names its own asset prompt and motion, so scripts/wick-explainer-assets.js can generate the whole film in one pass. `motion: video` shots cost Higgsfield credits; `motion: still` shots are illustrations driven by camera work, which is how real explainer channels do most of their runtime.

shots.vo: Your paycheck landed two weeks ago. Can you say where it went?
shots.art: A candle character standing alone in a dim apartment at night, looking down at a phone in his hand, the screen the only bright thing in the room. Wide shot, he is small in the frame, the room large and quiet around him.

shots.vo: Most people can name two or three things. The rest is a blur. That blur is the whole problem.
shots.art: The same candle character seen from behind, facing a wall covered in overlapping paper receipts and statements, all blank with no readable text, layered like wallpaper. Moody, warm lamp light from one side.

shots.vo: Here is what actually happens. The moment money arrives, it starts splitting.
shots.art: A candle character standing beside a large simple metal funnel on a plain table, watching a stream of warm golden light pour into the top of it. Clean, uncluttered, one object.

shots.vo: Rent and bills take the first cut. You expect that one. It is the only part most people can actually name.
Then comes the part nobody watches. Subscriptions. Fees. The upgrade you took last year and never used since.
And then there is the leftover. The amount you tell yourself you will save.
shots.art: A candle character looking into a wide shallow bowl on a kitchen counter with a single small coin at the bottom of it. Warm overhead light, the bowl mostly empty.

shots.vo: Here is why that never works. Leftover is not a plan. It is a remainder. And a remainder is whatever the month decides to leave you.
Every month you did not choose the number, the month chose it for you. Usually zero.
shots.art: A candle character standing in front of a large blank wall calendar, arms at his sides, looking up at it. The calendar grid is empty with no numbers or writing anywhere.

shots.vo: The fix is one move. Flip the order. Name the number first, and let the leftover be what it is.
Same paycheck. Same bills. The only thing that changed is which one got decided first.
So tonight, before you close your phone, set one automatic transfer for the day after you get paid. Any amount. The amount matters less than the order.
shots.art: A candle character sitting on the edge of a bed at night, phone held in both hands, the screen glowing warmly on his face. Calm and settled, the room dark around him.

shots.vo: You cannot save what is left. You can only save what you took first.
shots.onScreen: YOU CANNOT SAVE WHAT IS LEFT
shots.art: A candle character standing alone in warm morning light by a window, calm and upright, the room simple and uncluttered around him.
